extracted.intended_audience: Federal agency standards executives, rule writers, and program managers responsible for implementing the NTTAA and OMB Circular A-119
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and reporting expectations for Federal agencies on use, adoption, participation in, and replacement of voluntary consensus standards (VCS) under the NTTAA and OMB Circular A-119, including when government-unique standards may be used. Includes recommended procedures, tracking metrics, and examples of rationale for rejecting VCS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for voluntary consensus standards (VCS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must use international and national voluntary consensus standards in preference to Federal and agency standards, consistent with P.L. 104-113 and OMB Circular A-119.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implemented through departmental policies/orders (e.g., DOE Order 1300.2A) and program procedures; encourages staff participation in development and coordination activities of voluntary consensus standards committees. Agencies should routinely consider VCS in proposed and final regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and report use of government-unique standards in lieu of VCS
rubrics_metrics.description: P.L. 104-113 requires agencies to identify all instances when they use government-unique standards instead of voluntary consensus standards and to report the rationales and backgrounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must summarize instances (e.g., EPA, DOT, USDA examples) and explain why a VCS was rejected or unavailable. Reports include counts and narratives in annual reporting (see Table 1 format).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain rationale in rulemaking preambles when rejecting or considering VCS
rubrics_metrics.description: In Federal Register notices, rule writers should summarize the requirements of the NTTAA, explain how they searched for potentially applicable voluntary consensus standards, and describe their tentative or final decisions about the use of such standards in the regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA practice: nearly 100 FR documents included NTTAA preambles in FY1998; explanations should provide sufficient detail to show systematic assessment and rationale for decisions (e.g., impracticality, extra/unnecessary requirements, enforcement concerns).

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop and use model language and guidance for rule writers
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should develop a Rule-Writer's Guide and model language to explain NTTAA procedures and to facilitate consistent inclusion and electronic tracking of VCS consideration in rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA's draft 'EPA Rule-Writer's Guide to the NTTAA' explains procedures to systematically assess VCS application. Model language facilitates electronic tracking and annual reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track adoption, referencing, and staff participation metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should develop systems to track the adoption or referencing of voluntary standards and the level of staff participation in VCS developing bodies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested metrics (as in Table 1): number of voluntary consensus standards used since 10/97, change from prior year, number of agency employees participating, number of VCS bodies participated in, number of voluntary standards substituted for government-unique standards, number of government-unique standards used in lieu. Use electronic directories/databases for exchange and tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish agency standards policy, monitoring units, and infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should develop specific policy and programmatic elements to support implementation, including establishing agency standards policy and units for monitoring standards activities, resource allocation, infrastructure, reporting, and assessing program effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements for consideration: agency standards policy, dedicated units for monitoring, resource allocation plans, infrastructure for participation and tracking, reporting mechanisms, and program effectiveness assessment. NIST policy and template can be models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan and allocate resources and staff for standards participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should plan for resource and staff allocation for participation in appropriate voluntary consensus standards activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations emphasize strategic planning for agency participation, use of available resources (including NIST) to determine applicable SDOs and relevant voluntary standards, and budgeting for participation in standards committees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare and coordinate staff positions for standards committee participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop guidelines and training to prepare agency staff for participation in standards-related activities and coordinate positions with other Federal agencies so that Federal needs are reflected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines should reflect need to prepare views, coordinate inter-agency positions, consider appropriate agency role to avoid appearance of dominance, and consider likely future agency and national needs during development/revision of voluntary standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address ethics and conflict-of-interest issues for employee participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should reconcile criminal code provisions concerning financial conflicts of interest with the NTTAA directive that Federal employees participate in standards-setting activities, providing clear ethics guidance to permit appropriate participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA revised guidance (Sept 1998) relied on DOJ OLC and OGE memoranda to provide a clear pathway for employee membership in SDOs, including serving on boards and as committee chairs, while addressing conflict-of-interest concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use VCS where adequate; reject VCS only with documented, specific reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may reject a voluntary consensus standard when it is impractical for agency regulatory purposes due to reasons such as unnecessary additional requirements, ambiguous units leading to inconsistent application, or lack of necessary quality control/compliance criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA examples: ASTM D-3960 rejected in favor of EPA Method 24 because D-3960 had additional unnecessary requirements and unspecified units that could lead to inconsistent application and enforcement difficulties; Standard Methods 6640B tentatively rejected because sample preparation and QC procedures differed enough from EPA Method 515.1 to risk underreporting. Rejection decisions must be explained in the FR notice and agencies are encouraged to work with SDOs to resolve issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure testing/analytical methods meet agency QC and data verification needs
rubrics_metrics.description: If voluntary consensus standards lack standardized quality control and compliance criteria required for agency data verification and validation, agencies may develop or retain government-unique methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA found that none of several VCS alone met its water program needs for QC/compliance (leading to use of EPA Method 1650). Agencies should document such technical gaps when choosing government methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider practical user feedback (e.g., focus groups) vs VCS guidance on a case-by-case basis
rubrics_metrics.description: When stakeholder research (e.g., focus groups) yields results contrary to a voluntary consensus standard, agencies should make case-by-case determinations guided by agency expertise and mission differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHTSA example: focus groups preferred yellow headings though ANSI specified orange; the agency recognized differing missions (ANSI's broad hazard hierarchy vs focus groups' specific label effectiveness) and sought comments on which should guide final choices. Agencies should rely on expertise and judgment for such determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and replace government-unique standards with VCS where dual-use exists
rubrics_metrics.description: Departments (e.g., DOD) should review military specifications and standards to determine whether a replacement voluntary consensus standard already exists or could be developed, and plan for replacement to avoid proliferation of government-unique documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOD reviewed 30,000+ military specifications, adopted large numbers of VCS, and identified candidates for replacement; agencies should install procedures to prevent recurrence of unique-document proliferation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop government-unique standards only when no suitable VCS exists and plan for transition
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies may develop unique internal standards to consolidate practices, capture failure experience, or provide guidance where no suitable national/international standards are available, but should participate with industry/SDOs to transition such standards to VCS where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NASA developed IT, engineering, safety/mission-assurance standards for internal use or where VCS were unavailable; NASA is participating with industry and domestic/international VCS bodies to target standards for eventual transition to VCS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use public workshops and information sharing to support implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should host public workshops, summits, and seminars to share lessons learned, facilitate establishment or incorporation of coordinating organizations, and to acquaint stakeholders with revised Circular requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIST and DOE hosted workshops; NIST convened a summit 'Toward a National Standards Strategy'; DOE and other agencies used workshops to discuss implementation and share experiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt administrative tools to facilitate participation and information exchange
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies should develop electronic forms, directories, newsletters, and web resources to register and inform standards participants and provide current information on Federal standardization activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIST developed an electronic form for registering standards participants; recommendation that NIST consider a newsletter and web site; agencies encouraged to use electronic directories/databases to exchange standards-related information.
